A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the majority (83 per cent) of the sources have X-ray spectra that are consistent with heavily obscured power laws, while 14 per cent have additional soft components, and only a few sources (3 per cent) are BLAGN.

the majority of our sample are absorbed QSOs, and that there are a small number of broad-line QSOs which are either intrinsically weak soft X-ray sources, or which have an additional soft component that is absorbed by an ionized absorbers.

the XMM-Newton survey of hard X-ray-selected AGN shows that the X-ray spectra of most optically bright AGN are dominated by heavy absorption, that the X-ray-absorption column density is not correlated with the optical luminosity, and that the fraction of BLAGN with ionized absorbers is small.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the X-ray spectra and the optical properties of our sample are consistent with the picture in which AGN are divided into type 1 (broad-line) and type 2 (narrow-line), and that there is a strong correlation between the X-ray absorption and the optical classification.

the optical spectra of the optically bright X-ray sources are dominated by narrow lines, with only a small fraction of broad-line objects, in contrast to previous work which found a higher fraction of BLAGN.
, at least for the optically bright subsample, the X-ray hardness selection is a powerful method of selecting a sample with a high fraction of heavily absorbed AGN.
